title: KV-priority quanta and SLO governor for continuous batching
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and implement a new SLO-aware scheduling layer for the continuous batcher that enforces fairness across customers and decreases tail latency by combining token-quanta budgeting with KV cache locality heuristics and GPU memory compaction. This ticket covers the end-to-end work: design doc, prototype scheduler, KV reservation semantics, observer metrics, e2e load tests, and a staged rollout plan for runtime-1.21.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can assign token-quanta budgets per request and preempt running batches when higher-SLO work arrives within configured thresholds
KV cache soft-reservations allow hot-tenants to achieve >80% hit-rate for pinned prefixes while allowing eviction for emergency preemption
Tail P95 generation latency reduced by >=12% under mixed workload (tiered customers) compared to baseline continuous-batcher
GPU memory fragmentation reduced by periodic compaction with pause impact <2ms p99 across observed models
Feature gated and rolloutable: can be A/Bed and gradually enabled per-cluster via console rollout flags
design_decisions: Token-quanta: each request is mapped to a dynamic token budget based on SLO tier, estimated remaining tokens, and current sequence length distribution. Budgets are expressed in 'quanta' (coarse-grained token units) to keep scheduling cheap.

Proportional-share with decay: fairness attained by proportional-share across active tenants but with an aging factor that boosts recently-starved tenants to avoid starvation under sustained high-priority traffic.

KV soft-reservations: allocate a percentage of KV slab to tenant reservations (configurable), but mark as 'soft' so eviction can reclaim under emergency preemption. Soft-reservations track prefix-hotness and credit usage.

Cooperative preemption points: prefer to preempt at predefined yield points (end of decode step, before attention recompute) to avoid inconsistent KV state. Forced preemption uses checkpoint/restore-safe eviction only as fallback.
GPU memory compaction: incremental GPU-side compaction runs during low-activity windows; full compaction is avoidable by slab reuse + pinned-slab region for high-priority tenants.
Admission control: early reject/queue policy for requests that would exceed token budgets and lead to SLO violation; returns structured error with recommended backoff when queued beyond threshold.
Observability: expose per-tenant quanta consumption, eviction events, compaction pauses, preemption counts, and estimated remaining tokens via runtime metrics and per-route console panels.
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight quanta allocator in the continuous-batcher hot path: O(1) decision per request. Use precomputed estimates for token consumption from profiling histograms.
Extend KV cache metadata with tenant_id, prefix_score, last_access_ts, reserved_quanta and soft_reservation flag. Keep metadata compact (2-3 words) to avoid extra memory overhead.
Implement a 'yielder' interface in runtime kernels so models expose safe preemption points. Start with llamatype & transformer-family checkpoints we already support.
GPU compaction: leverage existing CUDA workstreams to run incremental compaction on a low-priority stream; schedule compaction only when GPU utilization <30% for >500ms.
Fallback preemption: implement a two-phase eviction: (1) mark for eviction and drain related KV references, (2) when safe, reclaim GPU memory. Track reclamation latency per eviction event.
Config knobs: per-cluster defaults, per-tenant overrides (for Dedicated customers), and per-route soft limits exposed via API/Console.
testing_plan: Unit tests for quanta allocator and proportional-share accounting under synthetic sequences.
Integration tests: multi-tenant scenario with mixed SLOs (gold/silver/bronze) reproducing prioritized arrivals and verifying preemption boundaries.
Stress tests on staging with worst-case KV churn (hot prefixes switching every 10s) to validate eviction/backoff behavior.
GPU memory tests: allocate test models with known fragmentation patterns, verify compaction reduces fragmentation and does not regress p50 latency.
Chaos test: randomly inject forced preemption and GPU compaction during heavy traffic to validate safety and observability.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged behind 'slo-quanta-scheduler' with default off for hosted clusters.
Phase 1 (internal): enable on 2 staging clusters with synthetic tenant mix and run for 1 week of continuous load.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of production traffic in a single region, monitor P95/P99, KV hit-rate, eviction rate for 48h.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): increase to 25% and then 100% if no regressions; enable per-tenant overrides for Dedicated customers earlier if requested.
Rollback criteria: any sustained >5% increase in P99 generation latency or >10% drop in KV hit-rate for a tenant triggers automatic rollback and incident page.
